Discussed root cause (KV cache eviction + autoscaler race on Dedicated pool), mitigations applied, proposed reliability improvements (runbooks, alert thresholds, fallback model routing), and next steps for benchmarks and evidence sharing.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-12-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), David Li (Zenith VP Eng), Aisha Khan (Zenith SRE), Tom Reynolds (Zenith Head Security), Priya Desai (Zenith Product)

Summary (auto): Follow-up on the 2027-11-29 production incident where latency spikes and 500s occurred for approx 18 minutes. Discussed root cause, mitigations, and concrete follow-ups.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we, uh, wanted to run through the postmortem follow-up and make sure we have clear action items. David, thanks for making time.
[00:12] David Li: Yeah thanks, thanks Maya. Appreciate the timeline from the on-call yesterday, we, uh, we got hit pretty hard, our customers noticed.
[00:20] Samir Gupta: Quick TL;DR before we go deep: root cause appears to be a KV cache eviction under heavy tail traffic combined with the autoscaler triggering a scale-up that briefly saturated the model warmup window, causing requests to fall back to the hot path and hit a higher latency and increased error rate.
[00:38] Aisha Khan: Sorry, can you say that again about warmup? We saw a ton of inflight requests spike and then 500s for about 15-18 minutes.
[00:46] Samir Gupta: Right, so in your Dedicated pool we saw a mix of very long context and short context requests. Our prefix caching had to evict some KV pages because of memory pressure, which increased the time to service those long contexts. At the same time, the autoscaler added nodes but model warmup (kernel selection+KV rehydration) lagged, so the scheduler rerouted some traffic to fallback instances which then queued up and produced 500s.
[01:05] Tom Reynolds: Is this a bug in the runtime or a capacity/configuration issue?
[01:10] Samir Gupta: It's mostly an orchestration/interaction issue. The runtime behaved as designed, kernel selection and quantized kernels are fine. The problem was the interaction between aggressive autoscale policy and our current KV eviction thresholds under your observed sequence-length distribution.
[01:25] David Li: Hmm. So practically, what changed for us? We want to know what we need to change in config vs what Redwood changes on your side.
[01:31] Maya Patel: Good question. Short answer: immediate config changes we recommended and pushed last week — we increased KVCache high-water mark, tightened eviction thresholds, and adjusted the autoscaler cooldown to be longer. Those reduced the window for warmup mismatch. On Redwood side we pushed a fallback improvement: better pre-warming heuristics and a patch to hold requests in a short buffer while the KV rehydrates instead of returning 500s right away.
[01:55] Aisha Khan: I saw the patch, thanks. There were still a few 500s after the patch until the cooldown settled.
[02:03] Samir Gupta: Yep, the patch reduces binary 500s but there's still some tail latency until the KV cache fully stabilizes; that's why we're recommending a runbook change and additional alerts.
[02:13] Priya Desai: For product, we need to know customer impact and whether we can avoid SLA credits.
[02:18] Lena Ortiz: We documented the user-facing impact in the postmortem; total affected traffic window was ~18 minutes, error rate peaked at 3.2% for a subset of heavy requests. We will provide the exact breakdown in the timeline doc.
[02:33] David Li: Ok, and the security folks requested all audit logs and we need to see KMS access pattern during the incident.
[02:40] Tom Reynolds: Yes, we need the Vault logs and any access to keys around that time. Also want to audit whether any fallback routing leaked data to other tenants — this was a concern in our legal review.
[02:52] Samir Gupta: Understood. We redacted tenant ids but we'll share full audit timeline and the KMS access entries; nothing indicates cross-tenant data exposure, but we'll give you the logs for your security team to verify.
[03:05] Maya Patel: We'll also provide the firewall and VPC flow summaries for the time range.
[03:12] David Li: Great. Can you run through the concrete reliability improvements you propose?
[03:18] Samir Gupta: Sure. High level: 1) Runbook and alerting: add a specific alert for KV eviction rate + inflight request queue length correlated with autoscaler events. 2) Autoscaler policy: increase cooldown and add a staged warmup policy so new nodes are gradually ramped into production traffic. 3) Pre-warming heuristics: proactively rehydrate KV for commonly used long prefixes during scale events. 4) Fallback routing: implement buffered short-hold for requests when KV rehydrate is in-progress to avoid immediate 500s. 5) Benchmarks: run dedicated capacity benchmarks with your workload and sequence-length distribution to validate thresholds.
[04:00] Aisha Khan: Benchmarks sound good—how much runway do we need? We want to simulate our peak (we saw 3x baseline for 6 minutes).
[04:08] Samir Gupta: We'll design a benchmark that reproduces your 3x spike and long-context mix. Expect me and your SRE to run it for 2-3 hours of tuning.
[04:17] Priya Desai: Is there any quick config we can do to avoid this in the short term aside from the eviction thresholds you changed?
[04:23] Maya Patel: Another short term knob is to pin critical routes to a small warm pool (a subset of nodes with higher KV margins) while we tune autoscaler. We can also create a rate-limited path for very long contexts.
[04:36] David Li: Ok, we'll consider pinned routes. On the legal side, Tom — any further asks?
[04:40] Tom Reynolds: We want SLA impact assessment and a written attestation that no PII was exposed. Also need confirmation of SOC2 controls for auditability on the fallback path.
[04:50] Lena Ortiz: We'll include the SLA impact calc in the customer postmortem and a security attestation from our compliance team.
[04:56] Samir Gupta: Quick note: we also found a configuration gap in the customer autoscale policy where the min nodes allowed a brief under-provision during rolling updates; we have a patch to that policy we've staged to your account.
[05:10] Aisha Khan: Was that a change made by our team or Redwood?
[05:13] Samir Gupta: It was a default policy that didn't match your burst profile; Redwood side we pushed a safer default for accounts flagged with heavy long-context traffic, but we need a confirmation to apply to your prod account.
[05:25] David Li: Please hold off until we sign off, but share the policy diffs.
[05:29] Maya Patel: We'll share them.
[05:31] [06:00] -- NOTE: gap in transcript due to transcription segfault -- resumed at 06:00 --
[06:00] Samir Gupta: Coming back, one thing we want to track for reliability is the prefix frequency heatmap; if we can get anonymized samples of your top prefixes, we can pre-warm proactively.
[06:12] David Li: We can ask product to provide that anon sample. We will need help redacting customer sensitive strings.
[06:18] Priya Desai: We'll prepare a redacted sample set.
[06:22] Tom Reynolds: Also please include the encryption-at-rest checks and verify no keys were rotated during the window.
[06:28] Samir Gupta: We'll include KMS timeline; nothing rotated during the window.
[06:33] Maya Patel: Ok wrapping to next steps: we agreed Redwood to share timeline + logs by Monday, benchmarks to be scheduled for the week of 12/12, and runbook proposals by 12/09. Any other questions?
[06:47] Aisha Khan: One ask—can Redwood provide a short-term mitigation script we can run from our side to increase KV memory allocation if we see early signs?
[06:55] Samir Gupta: Yes, we have a safe toggle script. We'll share the ops playbook for that.
[07:00] David Li: Great. We'll expect the docs and we'll review the benchmarking plan.
[07:06] Lena Ortiz: I'll follow up with the customer-facing note and timeline summary once you confirm access for logs.
[07:12] Tom Reynolds: Thanks everyone.
[07:14] Maya Patel: Thanks all. End of call.

Attachments/Refs: Postmortem doc link: https://redwood.company/pm/zenith-20271129 (redacted link). Benchmark spreadsheet: https://sheets.redwood.company/zenith-benchmark (access by request). Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521 (internal).
